review:
You spend the majority of your time sitting in a disgusting ditch filled with the shattered corpses of your fallen comrades, as well as those still unfortunate to be "alive", if you can even use that term to describe what is left of those wretches. As you crawl through soggy trenches, you can hear the shouts of orders being given and soldiers being slain, either blown to torn meat by mortar explosions or cut in half from machine gun fire. You are not a man, you are a frightened rabbit that dashes from cover to cover, whispering wishes of survival for but a few more seconds while pieces of concrete are chipped away around you by enemy sharp shooters. In the worst of times, you are a worm that crawls in the mud, lest a rifleman spots your shape in the distance. There is no salvation from a tank. Death can come from nowhere at all. 

Stay away fom windows.

Also, you can't drop more than five feet without breaking a leg. It's fine though, since your small pack of two bandages offers you a second chance at life. Try not too die to quickly, and remember to check your magazine. You can also modify your sights and give out commands. There are a variety of classes to choose from. Choose wisely, and don't be afraid to loot corpses; they don't need anything anymore anyway.

Stay away from windows. 

There is also a morale system, where you slowly lose your mind if you are under a barrage of enemy rounds, or if you see an ally get half of their face blown off and fall to the ground screaming in agony for a good minute or so before bleeding out. The result is blurred and discolored sight. I think I got this when I saw a guy get his legs shot off and watched him crawl about an inch away from cover before getting taken out by a sniper.

Stay away from windows.

In all seriousness, this game has a great deal of work put into detail and animations, but there remain some optimization issues. They're not bad, and a someone with an excellent PC might never even notice them.

Rising Storm and Red Orchestra 2 have different dynamics, although the mechanics are exactly the same, if that makes any sense. 

If there is one thing I have to ABSOLUTELY give this game credit for, is that it has a personality. A very grim personality, but it's better than the typical "fuck yeah" jingoism many games go for.

There is nothing more satisfying than watching an enemy tank blow to bits.

The singleplayer is good practice, but the AI is really ditzy. The soldiers do not show a lot of initiative and tanks commanders seem to forget that tanks can't climb walls.

Also, about the window thing: I was waiting for my squad to move up and about seven of them decided march right in front of a window in a factory. A machine gunner across the chasm opened up on them and killed them all. It was really unpleasant to watch them panic and stumble and run into each other while being shot to pieces.

A good WW2 FPS notable for it's high skill ceiling and one-hit deaths.

Stuff I like about this game:

-1-hit deaths. Seriously, (almost) every gun kills you in one-hit (besides the SMGs which might just wing you at longer ranges. This is a very realistic FPS.

-It doesn't hold back with how challenging it is. Working off of the 1-hit deaths, it made me legitimately SCARED when I first started out in the game. I would hide in artillery shell craters, prone to the ground, it was very immersive as a game that depicts the Eastern Front of WW2.

-Good class-based combat. You have: Riflemen who are guys who capture the objective. Squad Leaders who serve as a spawn point for everyone, throw smoke to conceal your team while they advance, and mark artillery bombardment locations. Machine gunners who lock down an area with 1-hit killing rapid-fire machine guns. Snipers who pick off priority targets from long range (machine gunners, squad leaders, other snipers, the Commander). Assaults who have close ranged weapons to clear buildings. And the Commander who play this game like an RTS, he orders recon planes, artillery, amoung other stuff.

-In conjunction with those classes and their roles, this game encourages team-play. No matter who you are, actually killing the enemy doesn't just get you a higher score. Killing the enemy IN the objective while STANDING in the objective though, DOES.

-Bullet trajectory. Bullets sink over longer distances and take time to reach the people you shoot at, there is no hitscan. Thank goodness, because this makes the game a bit more complex.

Downsides:

-Punishing for newer players. The other people playing probably know where to hide and you need to learn how to cope with the 1-hit kills. You get used to this over time, but just take my advice and play your first few hours as a simple Rifleman to just get the hang of everything.

-It's a bit janky. Sometimes I have to hit a key twice to do something, it lacks just a 'little' bit of polish. It doesn't break this game, it's just sometimes the controls fight with you a little bit.

tldr, This is a great realistic FPS that places a greater emphasis on playing the objective, being a sneaky sh*t who knows how to hide while shooting the enemy, and playing the specific role of your class. I reconmend it.

For anyone who wants to read a story about a valient battle and sacrifice, keep going. I'm just going to rant on about how much fun I've had with this game.

Our Russian army had decided to take the Bridges of Druzhnia (I think thats spelled right) against an overwhelmeng German force. The initial assault on A and B lasted nearly fourteen minutes and cost us nearly 150 reinforcements. Further attacks up past D and E cost us an additional hundred. Fueled by our losses, my Squad headed the assault on G, when the roar of The Buzzsaw was heard from the upstairs window. Rushing forward, we made it to the wall but at the cost of six good men. I sent my men on a dual flank before tossing a grenade through the upstairs window, watching as the LMG fell from the window followed by a grey-sleeved arm. Our Commander linked up with our group and commended us for our actions, before pushing us onward. The success of our assault with minimal casualties earned us a feared reputation and a simple, yet accurate nickname: Alpha Squad.

At this time, we quickly rushed our assault forward and knocked out the next positions with ease, until we came to the final bridge, section N. Fifteen minutes remained on the clock, and only a hundred of our reinforcements were still alive. We recieved an order from our commanding officer to halt, and recieved the most motivational speech of all time, as we prepared to fight against all odds. Once all of our teams were strategically placed, we recieved the final order to charge the position from three sides.

The following events took place over approximately ninety seconds:

Our original plan failed catastrophically. Our initial force was obliterated within seconds by the enemy artillery and machine guns. Two unnamed members of Alpha Squad plus myself and our MG moved underneath the bridge to hit with a surprise attack so that our engineer could take out the tank traps. The enemy fire was too intense however, so our engineer only had time to deploy the charges before a Buzzsaw across the river cut him down. During this time, our sniper and commander were to be located on our side of the bridge, laying down cover fire, but they were no match for the German beast and were forced to get into cover. The other four members of my squad were not so lucky, as they had just seen the flash before it ripped them to pieces.

While the suppressing group was pinned and taking heavy fire, the Germans brought their Antitank rifles out to take down our T34. However, my smoke grenade had impaired their ability to properly aim, and so fortunatley most of the shots missed the tank. However, the sniper was hit by one of these stray rounds - his body was only partially recovered. I felt tremendous guilt over the loss of a friend, but continued to push onward.

Our CO got right up in the action, using the tank as moving cover while he laid down fire with his PPSH. When that was empty, he simply tossed it to the side and pulled out his revolver. After being hit and bandaged three times; a shot to the right arm, one in the leg and another in the stomach; he was on the verge of dying. In his love for the mother country, he pulled out a grenade and rushed forward, taking two more Germans with him.

Our MG gunner used the distraction to set his position and took out seven Germans, including their Commanding Officer before a grenade landed just behind him. The explosion took off both of his legs and killed him outright, along with the other two soldiers that were coming up behind us. The blast also crippled my left arm, and in a fit of rage over my dying comrades, I didn't bother to bandage it. Being the final surviving member of the most elite fighters on the Eastern Front, I rushed forward with my PPSH, fully loaded with 71 rounds. It was my job to make sure that the tank made it to the final position, regardless of the cost. While firing at the exposed Germans, a sniper caught me in the chest with a single shot, which I immediatly knew would be fatal. The screen slowly faded to black, but my final breaths would not go silently. I died with my finger still squeezing the trigger, finishing off two more jackboots that tried to stop our desperate assault. Our sacrifice was minimal compared to the 800 Russians that were lost in the assault, but it had allowed enough time for our final remaining men to capture the position and win the game.

Red Orchestra 2 is pretty cool, I guess. I mean, if you like having post traumatic stress disorder.

RO2:RS:MTV, is the sequel to Red Orchestra, which in turn is a sequel to an Unreal tournament 2004 mod called Red Orchestra, which in turn is a prequel to Battlefield: bad company 2: Vietnam. 

The game takes place during WW2, a time in history when it was okay to wear a fedora, and it was only this time, so cut it out. Red Orchestra 2 focuses heavily on multiplayer, which is bad for me because that means I have to talk to people, which is bad for them because they can't understand meth induced slurring. Even with its multiplayer focus, the game manages to carry a narrative, and that narrative is "We should probably stop having these wars, guys."

The game takes no liberties with the horrors that are war, screams of pain are constant, cries for mercy will haunt you, and realism mode is so immersive you can smell the vodka off Gregor's breath.
For Christ sakes Gregor, brush your teeth you crazy Ivan. 

The game is not about ideologies, you won't be getting a Medal of Honor type story about how country A saved the world from country B. The game is about soldiers, the men who fought and died in the worlds biggest game of finger points. Bang Bang. 
None of the four factions involved are idolized or demonized. The game also has nation specific voices, so Germans speak German, Russians speak Russian, Americans speak American, and the Japanese speak in some language I've never heard of. Though I managed to pick up on some of their phrases. Like "Tuskete" means "Help me." and "Banzai" means "Put on some 3D glasses, because I'm coming right at you." 

But that aside, with all the blood and carnage and butt stabbing. Is the game fun to play? I would say yes.

It's an acquired taste, like beer or semen. It makes no efforts into easing in the casual crowed, or as I like to call them: the weak. 
It demands that you learn how to play it, it demands that you work together with your new virtual cartoon pals, and it demands that you learn how to use the rod that makes bullets magically appear to kill the people you're pointing at. I call them bang sticks. 

There is also a multiplayer campaign mode, which is probably the coolest idea a multiplayer game has had since Chromehounds, or Mech assault, or Armored Core. I would like more robots in my games please, but I digress. Players join a server and choose a side, this will be your side unless you're a filthy traitor and go turn coat. It adds a fictional narrative to a game about a real war, like American Marines defending Iwo Jima from a massive Japanese counter attack, or Russians once again fighting in Stalingrad against Super Hitler and his army of Nazi Zombies.
Somebody should a game about that, that sounds pretty cool, but I don't think Nazi Zombies™ would catch on.

Unlocking the frame rate: 

Locate the ROEngine.ini inside: "C:\Users\User\Documents\My Games\RedOrchestra2\ROGame\Config" open ROEngine with Notepad.

Locate a parameter that looks like this:

bSmoothFrameRate=TRUE
MinSmoothedFrameRate=22
MaxSmoothedFrameRate=62

Set "MaxSmoothedFrameRate=62" to "MaxSmoothedFrameRate=144" - I've used 144 as an example.

Note: Setting "bSmoothFrameRate=FALSE" will uncap the limit but you will only be able to get 90 frames.

Find the remaining MaxSmoothedFrameRate lines (use Ctrl + f) and set their values to the desired amount (there are 2 MaxSmoothedFrameRate and 2 bSmoothFrameRate to edit).

Now test using either the steam FPS overlay or alternatively open the console ingame with "~" and type in "Stat FPS".

This game, is an absolutely amazing game. It is set in and around Stalingrad, where the Germans and the Russians face off for victory. It is also set in and around the South-East Asian-Pacific region, where the Japanese and the Americans face off for victory. It is brutally realistic and gritty. A bullet from most weapons to the torso will kill you most of the time, same to the kneck or head. To the arms or legs most of the time it will wound you. Even if you are not killed after being wounded, if the wound is anywhere other than your limbs, you must patch yourself fast or you will bleed out, just like in reality. If it is in your limbs you may or may not bleed out, sometimes you have to judge if its better to run to cover and then heal, or heal on the spot and hope you don't get shot again. Or maybe you don't need to heal at all and you can save your bandages for worse wounds. The weapons have realistic recoil, and clear advantages and disadvantages for all situations. The Germans favor medium to long range fighting, the Russians medium to short range. The Germans and Russians are both perfectly capable of attacking and defending, but the Germans have an edge when it comes to attacking due to having longer ranged weapons, the only assault rifle in the world at the time, and machine guns with very high rates of fire that are very good for pinning the enemy down. The Russians have an edge on defense due to being good at letting the enemy come to them and grinding them down in close quarters fighting, along with the superior PPSH 41 sub machine gun, and superior mosin nagant bolt action rifle with its amazing accuracy that can blow the enemy away at close range even with sloppy aiming. Basically, some weapons for one side are superior to the other's equivalent. The audio in this game is stunning and extremely intense, much better than other shooters. This game is also extremely reliant on team work, no one-man armies allowed. If one team is communicating and working together, and the other is not, then the team that is working together will crush the other one. If both are doing what they are supposed to be doing then you get incredibly intense matches. 

The Rising Storm side of the game is pretty different from the Stalingrad part, for example Asymmetric warfare plays a huge role. The Japanese cannot face off against the Americans head on in open areas, the Americans just have too much fire power. The Japanese need to utilize the environment to keep mobility over the enemy and to take cover, jungle fighting is where they excell. All of the American riflemen have semi-automatic rifles, something neither the Japanese, nor the Germans or Russians get to have for their riflemen, and riflemen make up the bulk of the team. All of the other American classes have gear with superior raw damage and rates of fire to that of the Japanese, but what the Japanese excell at is their ferocity, combined with ingenious things such as creating frag grenade booby traps, knowing when to keep their distance so as to pick the enemy off from long range with their more accurate and longer range bolt action rifles, their knee mortars, and banzai charging in a small area in a big spearhead with smoke grenades and mortar/artillery/naval barrage support. The Japanese are definitely more geared towards attacking so as to hit the Americans on their terms and to overwhelm them in massed attacks, whereas the Americans, due to their superior raw fire power, are best on defense because they can dig in and if the Japanese run around in open areas they can mow them down like German machine guns on D-Day (Saving private Ryan style)

And speaking of D-Day, there is currently a 1944-1945 US vs German mod in development with testing events every few days, which will be like a fan made expansion which will bring the game up to 3 different theaters. 

And on top of that a World War I mod is in the early stages of development with both western and eastern front gameplay.

There are no hackers whatso ever, there are some modded maps that are optional to play on, and the vast majority of the player base are cool people, who don't mess around, are not casual, and who play to win, all of which creates an extremely intense gaming experiance.

I recommend it very highly. If you want a story-driven campaign, or good AI, or easy kills, look elsewhere. But give this a shot. It's so damn good. I've never been to war, and I'm so lucky to be able to say that. I'll never kill anybody in real life if I can help it. But this game took me out of my room and put me in the middle of the most brutal war in history better than any tightly-scripted CoD campaign ever could. Try it.

November 20, 1942
Modern Day Volgograd (Stalingrad)

Mortar shells rang in the frigid air. Artyom, Evgeny, and Sergei were huddled near a rock inside of a mortar hole. They each clutched rifles in their shivering hands. There was no emotion in their eyes. None but fear. Fear was what drove them to run through this blood-spattered, cold and unforgiving hell, and fear was what made them kill young men, young men who probably did not differ much from them.

They were the last remnants of their squadron, with the rest being gunned down in the the advance. The counter-offensive was in full storm, and the 3 were in a woeful spot. Alone in enemy territory, they stayed on alert inside of the mortar hole. Bodies of their comrades were littered, just metres away from the hole. If they dared to retrieve them, a swift bullet would be the reaction from the Germans, who had setup a machine gun post near the hole.

Eventually, after a few brief minutes of relative quiet (or what you would call quiet when your ears rang and artillery thundered miles away) they relaxed. Evgeny, the old seargent, took out a few cigarettes, and passed them around. Relieved, young Artyom and Sergei took them with gratitude, thanking him. They each lit their cigarettes over Evgeny's lighter. Smoking them, their minds calmed. It seemed that the Germans had thought all their number was wiped out, and were not going to send in an advance party to check the hole. For Evgeny, who realized it first, it seemed that atleast they would not be killed by advancing Germans for the moment. They all depended on their comrades in the back to come and rescue them now. And patience was soon wearing thin among the 3.

Whispering to not attract the attention of the Germans, Artyom started asking about Sergei's family, for lack of anything better to do.

"So, what was home like?" he asked.

Thinking back, 16 year old Sergei thought dreamily of his house on the hill, his brother who would run in the woods with him, the warm food served by mom, and the foolish things he did growing up.

"Well, I was born in Chelyabinsk, in the Urals. I grew up with my mother, father, and older brother. My father worked in the nearby factory, and me and my brother would play in the forest, chasing each other, throwing rocks at squirrels, and seeing who could climb the tallest trees. Our house was a cottage on a hill, with dozens of neighbours around us. The neighbours would sometimes join us when we played tag, or chased girls in the streets. But it all changed, soon. The houses were being emptied for suitable soldiers. The commisars said that they were being driven to fight "The Evil Fascist Scum", who they said were out for our homes, and it would be a most glorious way to help Comrade Stalin if we fought them. Everyone who looked 15 or older were taken, sometimes forcefully. My brother was one of them."

Sergei struggled to say any more. He held back tears in his eyes as he thought of his older brother.

"Dmitry was a tall, foreboding figure, but he was as kind. He wasn't the type of person to go to war and kill. But he got recruited nonetheless. I have not heard from him since, but I fear the worst."

He paused. He could speak no more.

"And what about you, Artyom? What was your home like?"

Artyom was contemplating memories, but right as he was about to say a word, a mortar round landed right near them, and a piece of steel shrapnel chopped off his head. Blood pooled around the headless body, and Sergei stumbled back, terrified.

"Artyom!?!?"

"GET DOWN!!" yelled Evgeny.

Shells started to strike left and right of the large mortar hole, creating scattered smaller ones.

Sergei and Evgeny ducked with their hands above their heads. The sound rang in their ears, like thunder and lightning. 

Evgeny thought about his wife and kids in Leningrad. He knew that he would probably never see them again. He had accepted this long ago. But now, in the storm of artillery, he could sense that the end was near.

Sergei could not remove the image of headless Artyom as he ducked and hoped that by some magic, the explosions would stop.

They didn't.









November 21, 1942

The squadron was moving up, now that the machine gun post had been bombed. They charged, bayonets out, into the Germans. Rifle fire mowed down many, leaving them to scream in the dirt and snow. Infront of the machine guns, was a mortar hole. Much of them dived into the mortar hole, to see 3 dead bodies. One has headless, with his head rolling around on the other side of the hole. Another died clutching his head, only to have a shrapnel round slice straight into it. The other one was lying, motionless, rifle in hand, and a photo of his wife in the other.

The following review is for Red Orchestra 2 and Rising Storm. (both included when buying Rising Storm)

Red Orchestra 2 and its stand-alone expansion Rising Storm are World War II military First-person shooters with an emphasis on solid gameplay mechanics and gritty authenticity. While the two differ in gameplay, both are grounded in realism without being marred by unnecessary clunkiness. Both were developed by Tripwire Interactive, the studio that is probably best known for Killing Floor and the original Red Orchestra game. Much like Killing Floor, these games shine most in the way that they feature what are quite possibly the best shooting mechanics that you will find in any video game.

These games are by no means "dead" as some doom-and-gloom internet posters would have you beleive. Despite featuring a complex set of controls and being fairly unforgiving about deaths in multiplayer, the games do a great job of expressing that the multiplayer expirience is hard but fair. Perceptivness, tactical forsight, and team communication are always heavily rewarding for players willing to go the extra mile. 

Much of the early criticism for Red Orchestra 2 by popular review sources and Metacritic mainly focus on the game's rough state at launch rather than the game you will be playing today. RO2 and RS have been greatly improved with the help of official patches and updates and even moreso with the help of the player community that is the backbone of the series. 

Rising Storm offers a new and different expirience to that of Red Orchestra 2. While still featuring the original game's brutality and satisfying gun mechanics, rising storm features more asymetrical gameplay that is more rooted in fast-paced action than the base game. This stand-alone expansion is great for both veterans looking for something fun and different as well as new players that felt intimidated by the heavily punishing nature of RO2's multiplayer. Upon purchasing Rising Storm players will recieve a copy of Red Orchestra 2 if they do not already own it. Red Orchestra 2 owners will be able to play a limited version of Rising Storm and will also recieve a discount when buying the expansion.

These games are great for anyone looking for a First-Person shooter with solid gameplay mechanics. Red Orchestra 2 and Rising storm offer a great experience that rivals and even surpasses those offered by AAA FPS titles.*


*The games are to be appreciated on their own merits rather than to be used to boost one's own ego for not being part of the Call of Duty or Battlefield audience.

Reviewing only Red Orchestra 2: Heroes of Stalingrad  - i did not own Rising Storm. 

RO2 is the dream of any hardcore WW2 fan. The game features battles from World War 2 between germans and the russians in Stalingrad. But why is it so great? 

That's simple: Because of the way they created it. You will fight in small troups as either normal soldier (only equipped with a Rifle and a Grenade) or as a special class, equipped with extra equipement. Mg's, Sniper, Tank destroyers, elite soldiers [..] There are various classes to choose from. But all of them are limtied, just like it was back then. The majority of players will always end up in the Rifleman Class. And that's good!

This is none of you usual run and gun games. It's a hardcore, challenging and very realistic team shooter. One shot to your chest? Likely dead. A shot to your arm? Well, yo can bandage that. A sniper bullet in your bottom? R.i.p. 
Gunplay is incredibly well made, reloading single bullets or clips is totally sufficient! The lack of an HUD just adds to the experience. 

The graphics are good! Not the best compared to today standards, but fitting to this kind of game. Dark atmosphere, dirty snow, dirty houses [...] Stalingrad lives again... 
The sound is one of the best i have ever experienced in an online shooter. While the normal shots are just your average sounds, its the overall package that makes it so great. Beeing shot at by an mg, jumping into cover, just to hear the player next to your dying slowly because he was hit by the bullets - you feel sad, angry and frightend. You don't want to peak out of cover when there is a sharpshooter ahead. You don't want to run through mg fire. You are afraid for your life. You are happy when you can get to the next trenches - it means there won't be anyoone able to snipe your head off. 
You will start to really feel like you are there, not just playing a game. 

The community is mostly very good! Roleplaying is not uncommon, neither is having great team leaders and commanders. Communication is proceeding smoothly, making it not only an fps, but also a strategical game. 

I could go on like this for hours, but let's just say: If you want a highly realistc, challenging world war 2 shooter, and don'tmind the high initial learning curve, this is for you! Buy it!

The game is fantastic. Great community, and the game is still amazing! It's perfect for those realism guys that play Arma and all but at the same time, they want to have some fun. Game is a mix of realism and fast paced balanced perfectly.

[h1]Welcome to the meat grinder[/h1]

If there is a game that can tell that you are nothing but meat in a war, it's this one for sure.
No game has ever given me the sense of morale, chills and terror as RO2.

When you join a 64 player server and a new map starts all you can hear is all your teammates charging to the objective, when you hear that you know that match needs to be won.
[b]In here you don't play for the kills, you play for the motherland/fatherland and your comrades that fight and die with you by your side.[/b]

[url=https://gfycat.com/EvilSpottedFieldspaniel]What it feels like when you start a new map in multiplayer[/url]

You can command your own Tank/Half-track (on certain maps that allow it) with different players occupying each role inside the vehicles, Yes you heard that right, no ridiculous 1 man inside tank that does-everything-at-same-time-shit here. Your tank driver gets shot? Too bad, you have to move yourself to the driver seat and use the vehicle with a less than adequate crew count.

Being a machine gunner in this game is really fun, specially when you can use MG's like [url=https://youtu.be/aZIQxbOsNiU?t=2m15s]MG42[/url] that shred any Yuri on its path and the pure terror of the gun firing so many rounds is incredible. The game has a very nice mechanic where your gun barrel can get extremely hot and break the gun if you fire too much, too fast, requiring you to switch out the barrels.

You don't find your usuall CSGO/COD kid here. The rambo gameplay that works on other games will never work here. That's a bonus right there.

It is a blast playing with good Team Leaders. They use their brain to strategically order heavy artillery on a fortified area via radio & relay orders to squad leaders to go attack/defend certain locations via voice chat.

The game has actual suppresion mechanics. If you fire at a sandbag cover for example where 2 enemies reside, their vision will become extremely blurry/hazed/fuzzy and gray. This allows you to cover fire your teammates just by firing enemies cover while they move up.

Last but not least, the sounds. The sounds man... Rarely a game ever gives you detailed sounds of everything happening around you like this. Artillery sounds, bullet cracks, dying sounds, the vehicles.

With all this you got an authentic WW2 simulator.
If there was a version of this game with official developed VR support, you could probably get [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b3K0tI-EyGY]PTSD[/url] from play this in just a couple hours.

[b]Game is worth every $.[/b] (Also note that every dlc has been free)

Let's start with the “Meh”: the game's singleplayer mode is the biggest, if not only, weakness of this title. They try to make a story around it, but it feels and plays identical to the Multiplayer. In that respect, the SP part feels more like "training with bots" than anything else. But that's because it is.

The real meat and bones of this juicy, juicy bean stew is in the multiplayer and I dare say that RO2 is the only title that has been able to display accurately the feel and struggle of the Second World War. Besides the maps and weapons and guts flying in all directions when a grenade lands, and all the bolt-action weapons, RO2 capture the essence of World War II by genuinely not giving a flying f*ck about the player.

No, really. Everything in this game is created with the precise reason of making your life hard and it works on so many levels.

 The movement is rough, with any sprint taking from your stamina bar, making it harder to aim. Entering or exiting crouch or prone will make you lose control of your weapon for a few seconds. Gone are the days of the Battlefield 3+ super soldier who could run, jump, sprint and crouch quicker than you can say “I wish they didn’t close the BF2142 servers”.
 Nearby artillery or enemy gunfire will also make your stamina deplete faster. When it gets to zero, your screen turns black and white and you can no longer zoom in while aiming; making shooting a more difficult endeavour.
 And a difficult one it is nonetheless; aiming is done in the usual modern manner, but with an extra twist. You can do a slight zoom while aiming down the sight, vital for the large fields that fill the RO2 maps (players of Operation Flashpoint 1 / Arma will know this feature). Trust me, you will need this slight zoom. On many maps, discerning a distant player from friend or foe is a challenge within itself and at first you will find yourself shooting friendlies in this game (remember to say “sorry”), but that is part of war, for war is gruesome.

 But perhaps the most authentic feature that strives to the game’s reality is it’s class system. In RO2, classes are restricted. Each map has x snipers, y gunners, z heavy gunners and so forth. These numbers are always small (less than 5), with the bulk of the players filling the most used class, Rifleman. This means that most players in a server will be using bolt-action rifles, while the more complex ones will have access to better weapons or tools/traits. This also highlights one of the game’s weaker points, since, without a pretty strong machine and gaming rig, your map will load slowly, lessening your chances of choosing the desired class.

Even so, I cannot recommend RO2 enough. It is a gem among 64-player FPS games and should be experienced by anyone who is interested in massive multiplayer shooters. The core game, along side with the Rising Storm expansion and the free maps created by the community give you a game that is still played thoroughly, for good reason.

Those games are designed for players who want quick action and instantaneous satisfaction.  Rising Storm is a FPS who likes to think and play tactically; if you want a game that facilitates running and gunning, high kill streaks and corny achievement states, look elsewhere.

There is a single player aspect, but multiplayer mode is the main reason to get and play this game.  The aspects that distinguish this game from other FPS’s:
•	You have to respect death.  If you run around without any awareness of the enemy’s disposition and cover, you’ll die frequently and quickly.  The cover mechanic and use of smoke, both from direct fire and indirect fires are big aspects of this game, and you must learn to move in a fashion that minimizes your exposure to such dangers.
•	You have to play to your role.  You can carry more than 1 primary weapon, but doing so will greatly slow you down.  So outside of playing in a defensive position, you won’t find it useful to Rambo around with two different weapons.  Whichever role you join in as, you need to learn how to play it effectively.  A rifleman’s job is to attack/defend objectives and to support the Squad leader’s intent.  An automatic rifleman or machine gunner is there to provide fire suppression in support of the team objectives.  A squad leader provides smoke cover and coordinates reinforcements.  Platoon leader directs fire support and overall squad maneuvers.  There are other job descriptions which the player will learn.  The player must play to his role.  A rifleman hanging back and shooting from afar does little for the team.
•	You have to be a team player.  Unlike other FPS shooters will people tend to run around looking for opportunities to improve their stats, this game demands that players work for the greater good of their team, sometimes to their own detriment.  You have to go after the objectives that the platoon and squad leaders direct you too.  Whether its rushing into a capzone through enemy fire or holding down a defensive position even after the enemy has cut off reinforcements, the best gameplay comes about when players actually work towards the team’s goals rather than for individual goals.  The squad leader and platoon leader command structure really facilitates this style of gameplay.
•	The gameplay is asymmetrical.  For the Japanese versus Americans, the Japanese have inferior firearms (generally-speaking) but a fearsome Banzai charge which suppresses enemy forces and allows them to charge into melee ignoring some amount of enemy fire.  They also have knee mortars and booby traps which can be an absolute nightmare for American teams in the right hands.  The Americans have a better selection of firearms, to include more automatic weapons and flamethrowers which can devastate Japanese charges if used properly.  For the Germans versus Soviets, the role and firearm options are somewhat similar, but there are minute differences here and there with employment methods.  A big reason why this game is so engaging is because the player has to learn to play his role and then learn how to play his role for the different team setup’s.  
•	The overall experience is quite immersive.  Between the blurred vision when suppressed (by banzai charges, artillery or machinegun fire), the sounds (weapons sounds are accurate and sounds reverberate when inside buildings) and the visual effects, this game really creates an immersive experience.  When the player plays to his role and works with the team, these immersive factors truly enhance the game’s overall engagement.  

There has been some let down with regards to this game: lack of player-created maps and mods; lack of armored vehicles and tanks (only a few maps have tanks); lack of developer attention after release.  But overall this game is a top quality product and well worth the money for anyone who wants a FPS WWII experience.

Red Orchestra 2 is a fantastic fps game.

Like few others, it walks the dangerous tightrope between realism and arcadey fun.
The high respawn rate and massive waves means that the game is not as tense as games like 'Insurgency' but is much much faster-paced.
It can be frustrating in early playthroughs as you die very quickly - especially to unseen enemies - but slowly, you can learn ways of keeping yourself safe from enemy fire.

The class system works best when there are large teams with players filling each role. Most players are riflemen, restricted to their humble bolt-action rifle and explosive grenades. It can be very tempting to move to classes with cooler toys but these often come with more responsibilities like commanding squads, spotting enemies, calling in artillery and mortar fire, and laying smoke. This reflects the real-life structure of these armies and is a more subtle counterpart to Overwatch or TF2 style class system.

Maps have wide degrees of variety and encourage all sorts of game play. There are many avenues for attack and defense and, within a single map, change from wide open spaces to dense city streets or even firefights within single large buildings such as the grain elevator. They also eschew the tendency for drab greyness, and manage to create realism with a bright colour palette from time to time, especially in rising storm.

If you:
- enjoy military realism
- want fast-paced tactical team action
- have patience for challenging mechanics
- enjoy the feeling of being in a large scale battle
BUY THIS GAME

--------[u]The Following Narrative Actually Happen in Red Orchestra 2[/u]---------

--------------------[u]Bridges of Druzhina - 1942[/u]--------------
Russians...Russians are everywhere. They took objective A, B, and C so quickly that our fellow soliders began to panic. My Honor Rank is 73 and a squad leader for Squad Two. I ordered my men to fall back to Objective G, the outskirts of Druzhina, and command them to fortify the position. Squad One fought valiantly against the Russians on Objective D, but most of them were wiped out. The dense forest that cover Objective D and E favor the Russians than our German forces. The Bolsheviks were clever to use smoke grenades to advance their position while our men fired wildly into the thick, white smoke. What are they shooting at? Who knows. 

As Objective E was spammed with Russians, the commander order the squad leaders, including me, to send in artillery coordinates. Unfortunately, there were too many artillery requests sent to the commander. The first coordinate is at the Russians on Objective E, the second coordinate is pointed directly at the Russian T-34, and the third coordinate was sent in close to Objective G. I was the one who sent in the third coordinate. I debated with my commander that the third coordinate is the best because the Russians would most likely be sending 2/3 of their forces to take G. The commander didn't listen and called the artillery at the first coordinate. As the artillery roars the sky and slams into the ground, the Russians were clever to run away from Objective E. Some of them died while the rest who were at Objective E rush to Objective G in a frontal assault. The machine gunner in my squad, whose Honor Rank is 58, fired his MG-34 in a control burst, but was killed by a sniper from 148 meters. I watch the machine gunner got shot and his body slump into the fragile, wooden floor. I was traumatized by this and order my men to not be exposed by the window. The rest of my squad consist of newer members, ranging the Honor Rank from 12 - 36 didn't listen to my command. The second squad member (Honor Rank - 26) was killed by the same sniper. 

Two squad members killed and the Russians are swarming in front of the sandbags near Objective G...and I have to make a choice. I ordered my squad to suppress fire at the Russians while waiting for additional reinforcements to come and defend Objective G. Unfortunately, the Bolsheviks pulled a hard, right flank at Objective F, wiping out Squad Three in under 20 seconds. Even though my squad was able to pluck a few kills around Objective G, the Russians purposely made this frontal assault as a distraction so that their comrades can take Objective F. Knowing that Objective G would be overrun from the right side, I ordered my lower ranking members to retreat back to the apartments in Objective I. Strangely, there were signs of courage and fury in my men's eyes. One of the squad members (Honor Rank - 21, Anti-Tank class) demanded me to let him risk his own life as the T-34 rushes to the main road that leads to Druzhina. I refused in his request and ordered him to tactically withdraw, but he didn't listen. Before I was about to demand an order to him, he pulls out the Hafthohlladung anti-tank grenade and runs directly in front of the T-34. He starts to scream and was about to swing the grenade, but was mowed down in a hail of machine gun fire from the Russians. However, I heard an explosion and I took a slight peak in the window. The T-34's main gun was pointing in front of me and the last I said to my men is: Run! This is Red Orchestra 2. 

------------------------------[u]Review[/u]----------------------------
Red Orchestra 2 is the ultimate first-person tactical shooter that advocate very strong team coodination and communication, complex cover system, and each life (or ticket) is precious. When playing as the Russian, German, American, or Japanese, each solider fight just to survive. There will be instances in the game that discourage reckless assaults or exposure to the enemy. You will learn the game by experience and not repeating the same mistakes twice. There are weapons, class, and character rankings that encourages replay value. The best experience you will get in Red Orchestra 2 is playing on a full server. You will hear the best team coordination, the best varieties of newer and veteran players, and the greatest responsibility for your own life and theirs. Red Orchestra 2 does not shy away from the actuality of war as you will hear meeps, horrific groans, and the development of post-traumatic stress disorder. There is no "I" in war; there is brother and comrade. Red Orchestra 2 is simply, the best tactical first-person shooter to ever develop.
